27: // resource configuration structures to nodes that implement
28: // GraphNodeAttachManagedResourceConfig or GraphNodeAttachDataResourceConfig.
29: //
30: // The attached configuration structures are directly from the configuration.
31: // If they're going to be modified, a copy should be made.

33: 	Config *configs.Config // Config is the root node in the config tree

35: 	// base is an alternate configuration tree used to resolve resource
36: 	// addresses when Config is unset.

41: 
42: 	// Go through and find GraphNodeAttachResource

45: 		arn, ok := v.(GraphNodeAttachResourceConfig)
46: 		if !ok {

48: 		}
49:

52:

54: 		config := t.Config.Descendent(addr.Module)

59: 		}
60:

62: 			log.Printf("[TRACE] AttachResourceConfigTransformer: attaching to %q (%T) config from %#v", dag.VertexName(v), v, r.DeclRange)

78: 	// A data source that is no longer in the config is removed from the state

81: 	// we need to update both the refresh state to refresh the current data

91: func (n *NodePlannableResourceInstanceOrphan) managedResourceExecute(ctx EvalContext) (diags tfdiags.Diagnostics) {
92: 	addr := n.ResourceInstanceAddr()
93: 
94: 	oldState, readDiags := n.readResourceInstanceState(ctx, addr)
95: 	diags = diags.Append(readDiags)
96: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
97: 		return diags
98: 	}
99: 
100: 	// Note any upgrades that readResourceInstanceState might've done in the
101: 	// prevRunState, so that it'll conform to current schema.
102: 	diags = diags.Append(n.writeResourceInstanceState(ctx, oldState, prevRunState))
103: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
104: 		return diags
105: 	}
106: 	// Also the refreshState, because that should still reflect schema upgrades
107: 	// even if not refreshing.
108: 	diags = diags.Append(n.writeResourceInstanceState(ctx, oldState, refreshState))
109: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
110: 		return diags
111: 	}
112: 
113: 	var forget bool
114: 	for _, ft := range n.forgetResources {
115: 		if ft.Equal(n.ResourceAddr()) {
116: 			forget = true
117: 		}
118: 	}
119: 	for _, fm := range n.forgetModules {
120: 		if fm.TargetContains(n.Addr) {
121: 			forget = true
122: 		}
123: 	}
124: 	var change *plans.ResourceInstanceChange
125: 	var pDiags tfdiags.Diagnostics
126: 	var deferred *providers.Deferred
127: 	if forget {
128: 		change, pDiags = n.planForget(ctx, oldState, "")
129: 		diags = diags.Append(pDiags)
130: 	} else {
131: 		change, deferred, pDiags = n.planDestroy(ctx, oldState, "")
132: 		diags = diags.Append(pDiags)
133: 
134: 		if deferred != nil {
135: 			ctx.Deferrals().ReportResourceInstanceDeferred(n.Addr, deferred.Reason, &plans.ResourceInstanceChange{
136: 				Addr:   n.Addr,
137: 				Change: change.Change,
138: 			})
139: 			return diags
140: 		}
141: 	}
142: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
143: 		return diags
144: 	}
145: 
146: 	if !n.skipRefresh && !forget {
147: 		// Refresh this instance even though it is going to be destroyed, in
148: 		// order to catch missing resources. If this is a normal plan,
149: 		// providers expect a Read request to remove missing resources from the
150: 		// plan before apply, and may not handle a missing resource during
151: 		// Delete correctly.  If this is a simple refresh, Terraform is
152: 		// expected to remove the missing resource from the state entirely
153: 		refreshedState, deferred, refreshDiags := n.refresh(ctx, states.NotDeposed, oldState, ctx.Deferrals().DeferralAllowed())
154: 		diags = diags.Append(refreshDiags)
155: 		if diags.HasErrors() {
156: 			return diags
157: 		}
158: 
159: 		diags = diags.Append(n.writeResourceInstanceState(ctx, refreshedState, refreshState))
160: 		if diags.HasErrors() {
161: 			return diags
162: 		}
163: 
164: 		// If we refreshed then our subsequent planning should be in terms of
165: 		// the new object, not the original object.
166: 		if deferred == nil {
167: 			oldState = refreshedState
168: 		} else {
169: 			ctx.Deferrals().ReportResourceInstanceDeferred(n.Addr, deferred.Reason, &plans.ResourceInstanceChange{
170: 				Addr: n.Addr,
171: 				Change: plans.Change{
172: 					Action: plans.Read,
173: 					Before: oldState.Value,
174: 					After:  refreshedState.Value,
175: 				},
176: 			})
177: 		}
178: 	}
179: 
180: 	// If we're skipping planning, all we need to do is write the state. If the
181: 	// refresh indicates the instance no longer exists, there is also nothing
182: 	// to plan because there is no longer any state and it doesn't exist in the
183: 	// config.
184: 	if n.skipPlanChanges || oldState == nil || oldState.Value.IsNull() {
185: 		return diags.Append(n.writeResourceInstanceState(ctx, oldState, workingState))
186: 	}
187: 
188: 	// We might be able to offer an approximate reason for why we are
189: 	// planning to delete this object. (This is best-effort; we might
190: 	// sometimes not have a reason.)
191: 	change.ActionReason = n.deleteActionReason(ctx)
192: 
193: 	// We intentionally write the change before the subsequent checks, because
194: 	// all of the checks below this point are for problems caused by the
195: 	// context surrounding the change, rather than the change itself, and
196: 	// so it's helpful to still include the valid-in-isolation change as
197: 	// part of the plan as additional context in our error output.
198: 	diags = diags.Append(n.writeChange(ctx, change, ""))
199: 	if diags.HasErrors() {
200: 		return diags
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	if !forget {
204: 		diags = diags.Append(n.checkPreventDestroy(change))
205: 		if diags.HasErrors() {
206: 			return diags
207: 		}
208: 	}
209: 
210: 	return diags.Append(n.writeResourceInstanceState(ctx, nil, workingState))
211: }

213: func (n *NodePlannableResourceInstanceOrphan) deleteActionReason(ctx EvalContext) plans.ResourceInstanceChangeActionReason {
214: 	cfg := n.Config
215: 	if cfg == nil {
216: 		if !n.Addr.Equal(n.prevRunAddr(ctx)) {
217: 			// This means the resource was moved - see also
218: 			// ResourceInstanceChange.Moved() which calculates
219: 			// this the same way.
220: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseNoMoveTarget
221: 		}
222: 
223: 		return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseNoResourceConfig
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	// If this is a resource instance inside a module instance that's no
227: 	// longer declared then we will have a config (because config isn't
228: 	// instance-specific) but the expander will know that our resource
229: 	// address's module path refers to an undeclared module instance.
230: 	if expander := ctx.InstanceExpander(); expander != nil { // (sometimes nil in MockEvalContext in tests)
231: 		validModuleAddr := expander.GetDeepestExistingModuleInstance(n.Addr.Module)
232: 		if len(validModuleAddr) != len(n.Addr.Module) {
233: 			// If we get here then at least one step in the resource's module
234: 			// path is to a module instance that doesn't exist at all, and
235: 			// so a missing module instance is the delete reason regardless
236: 			// of whether there might _also_ be a change to the resource
237: 			// configuration inside the module. (Conceptually the configurations
238: 			// inside the non-existing module instance don't exist at all,
239: 			// but they end up existing just as an artifact of the
240: 			// implementation detail that we detect module instance orphans
241: 			// only dynamically.)
242: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseNoModule
243: 		}
244: 	}
245: 
246: 	switch n.Addr.Resource.Key.(type) {
247: 	case nil: // no instance key at all
248: 		if cfg.Count != nil || cfg.ForEach != nil {
249: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseWrongRepetition
250: 		}
251: 	case addrs.IntKey:
252: 		if cfg.Count == nil {
253: 			// This resource isn't using "count" at all, then
254: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseWrongRepetition
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		expander := ctx.InstanceExpander()
258: 		if expander == nil {
259: 			break // only for tests that produce an incomplete MockEvalContext
260: 		}
261: 		insts := expander.ExpandResource(n.Addr.ContainingResource())
262: 
263: 		declared := false
264: 		for _, inst := range insts {
265: 			if n.Addr.Equal(inst) {
266: 				declared = true
267: 			}
268: 		}
269: 		if !declared {
270: 			// This instance key is outside of the configured range
271: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseCountIndex
272: 		}
273: 	case addrs.StringKey:
274: 		if cfg.ForEach == nil {
275: 			// This resource isn't using "for_each" at all, then
276: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseWrongRepetition
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		expander := ctx.InstanceExpander()
280: 		if expander == nil {
281: 			break // only for tests that produce an incomplete MockEvalContext
282: 		}
283: 		insts := expander.ExpandResource(n.Addr.ContainingResource())
284: 
285: 		declared := false
286: 		for _, inst := range insts {
287: 			if n.Addr.Equal(inst) {
288: 				declared = true
289: 			}
290: 		}
291: 		if !declared {
292: 			// This instance key is outside of the configured range
293: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseEachKey
294: 		}
295: 	}
296: 
297: 	// If we get here then the instance key type matches the configured
298: 	// repetition mode, and so we need to consider whether the key itself
299: 	// is within the range of the repetition construct.
300: 	if expander := ctx.InstanceExpander(); expander != nil { // (sometimes nil in MockEvalContext in tests)
301: 		// First we'll check whether our containing module instance still
302: 		// exists, so we can talk about that differently in the reason.
303: 		declared := false
304: 		for _, inst := range expander.ExpandModule(n.Addr.Module.Module(), false) {
305: 			if n.Addr.Module.Equal(inst) {
306: 				declared = true
307: 				break
308: 			}
309: 		}
310: 		if !declared {
311: 			return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseNoModule
312: 		}
313: 
314: 		// Now we've proven that we're in a still-existing module instance,
315: 		// we'll see if our instance key matches something actually declared.
316: 		declared = false
317: 		for _, inst := range expander.ExpandResource(n.Addr.ContainingResource()) {
318: 			if n.Addr.Equal(inst) {
319: 				declared = true
320: 				break
321: 			}
322: 		}
323: 		if !declared {
324: 			// Because we already checked that the key _type_ was correct
325: 			// above, we can assume that any mismatch here is a range error,
326: 			// and thus we just need to decide which of the two range
327: 			// errors we're going to return.
328: 			switch n.Addr.Resource.Key.(type) {
329: 			case addrs.IntKey:
330: 				return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseCountIndex
331: 			case addrs.StringKey:
332: 				return plans.ResourceInstanceDeleteBecauseEachKey
333: 			}
334: 		}
335: 	}
336: 
337: 	// If we didn't find any specific reason to report, we'll report "no reason"
338: 	// as a fallback, which means the UI should just state it'll be deleted
339: 	// without any explicit reasoning.
340: 	return plans.ResourceInstanceChangeNoReason

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `AttachResourceConfigTransformer.Transform` (internal/terraform/transform_attach_config_resource.go:40): removed blocks were only looked up within the config module matching the resource's own module path. When the resource lived in a module that was removed from configuration (e.g. `module.null.null_resource.main`), `Descendent(addr.Module)` returned nil and the `removed` block (declared in the root module) was never attached, so its destroy provisioners were never executed.

The fix collects all `removed` blocks from the entire config tree (`Config.DeepEach`) into an address-keyed map up front and attaches the matching one to each resource node before the module-descendant lookup, mirroring the upstream Terraform fix.
